title: Visual direction from brand personality
when: The user describes a feeling (playful, premium, trustworthy, rustic) and wants it turned into concrete visual choices before building.
inputs: what the brand must not feel like
prompt:
Goal: A one page direction that maps three personality words to concrete color, type, shape, imagery and motion values.
Steps:
1. Collect the audience, three personality words and one anti word (not childish, not corporate).
2. Translate each word into decisions: premium means generous space, serif headings, a deep neutral with one rich accent; playful means round radius, saturated accent, short bouncy motion.
3. Fix the decisions as values: two or three hex colors, the font stacks, radius and shadow level, image style (people photos, flat illustration, none).
4. Write do and do not pairs (Do: large photos of real people. Do not: stock icons in circles).
5. Check accessibility up front: contrast of the chosen pairs, readable sizes, motion that can be reduced.
6. Style a tiny sample (a hero and one card) with the values to confirm it reads right.
Quality bar:
- Every word maps to at least two values.
- Few, consistent choices.
- The sample passes contrast.
Pitfalls:
- Mood words with no values attached.
- Trendy effects that fight the personality.
- Five fonts for five adjectives.
Verify:
- [ ] Words and anti word stated.
- [ ] Color, type, shape, imagery and motion decided.
- [ ] Do and do not list present.
- [ ] Sample uses the values.
Output: direction.md starting with a # heading, plus sample.html and style.css for the sample.

examples.input: quero um visual rustico e acolhedor para minha pousada
examples.output: warm off white, olive accent #4f5d2f, serif headings, soft 8px radius, natural photos, slow fades
